text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- The president and judge of the Supreme Court, Krunislav Olujic removed from his post until disciplinary proceedings against him are over.
- What have state auditors found out while investigating the work of the ministries?
- How much will the wages go up on January 1?
- The Austrians to complete the construction works of the Plomin 2 thermo electric plant.
- The postponement of VAT a big mistake, says professor Manfred Rose, advisor to Croatia's tax reform.
- Privatisation minister Ivan Penic claims that 54 percent of the estmated value of capital has been privatised, while some economists say that the state still controls 80 percent of the economy.
- At it's today's session the parliament's house of counties to also discuss the Zagreb crisis.
- Croatian top economists agree that the current overappreciated kuna rate is killing Croatian economy. -- Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
